subject: math
title: Absolute Value and Ordering Rational Numbers
seo_title: Grade 6 Absolute Value Worksheets: Compare and Order Rational Numbers on a Number Line
standard_text: Understand ordering and absolute value of rational numbers.
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 absolute value worksheets: compare negative numbers with < and >, order integers, decimals and fractions, find absolute value as distance from 0, and solve temperature, debt and elevation word problems. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Farther right means greater. Absolute value is the distance from 0.
key_sub: −7 < −3 because −7 is farther left, but |−7| > |−3| because −7 is farther from 0. An absolute value is never negative.
body_html:
Order on the number line

On a number line, numbers get greater as you move to the right. A number to the left is less. This is true for negative numbers, too.

Write the result with a symbol. < means “is less than.” > means “is greater than.” The symbol opens toward the greater number.

Example

Compare −3 and −7.

−3 is to the right of −7. So −3 is greater. Both are negative, so the one closer to 0 is greater.

Answer: −3 > −7

Example

Compare −1.5 and 0.5.

Every negative number is to the left of 0, and 0.5 is to the right of 0.

Answer: −1.5 < 0.5

Order a list

To order numbers from least to greatest, put them in order from left to right on a number line. Write fractions as decimals when the list mixes them.

Example

Order from least to greatest: 2, −34, −1.5, 0.

−34 = −0.75. The negative numbers come first. −1.5 is farther from 0 than −0.75, so it is less.

Answer: −1.5, −34, 0, 2

Absolute value is distance from 0

The absolute value of a number is its distance from 0. We write it with bars: |−5| is read “the absolute value of −5.” Distance is never negative, so an absolute value is never negative.

NumberDistance from 0Absolute value
−88 units|−8| = 8
88 units|8| = 8
−2.52.5 units|−2.5| = 2.5
00 units|0| = 0

Absolute value is not the same as order

For negative numbers, a greater absolute value means a lesser number. −12 is farther from 0 than −5, so |−12| > |−5|. But −12 is to the left of −5, so −12 < −5.

Example

A balance of −$30 and a balance of −$20. Which is the bigger debt?

|−30| = 30 and |−20| = 20. The debt is the absolute value. The balance −$30 is less, but the debt is greater.

Answer: a debt of $30 is more than a debt of $20, and −$30 < −$20

Example

It is −4 °F in one town and 2 °F in another. Which town is colder?

−4 is to the left of 2, so −4 < 2. The lower temperature is colder.

Answer: the town at −4 °F

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Thinking −7 > −3 because 7 > 3Look at the number line: −7 is farther left, so −7 < −3
Writing |−8| = −8Absolute value is a distance: |−8| = 8
Ordering by absolute value: −1, 2, −5Order by position: −5, −1, 2
Mixing up < and >The symbol opens toward the greater number: −3 > −7
Counting tick marks instead of spaces|−6| is 6 spaces from 0, not 7 marks
Thinking the bigger debt is the greater balance−$30 is a bigger debt than −$20, but −$30 < −$20

faq.q: What is absolute value in 6th grade math?
faq.a: The absolute value of a number is its distance from 0 on the number line. |−8| = 8 and |8| = 8, and an absolute value is never negative.
No. −7 is to the left of −3 on the number line, so −7 < −3. A negative number farther from 0 is less.

faq.q: How do you order negative numbers from least to greatest?
faq.a: Put them in order from left to right on a number line. The negative number farthest from 0 comes first, and positive numbers come after 0, for example −5, −1, 0, 2.

faq.q: What is the difference between comparing numbers and comparing absolute values?
faq.a: Comparing numbers asks which is farther right; comparing absolute values asks which is farther from 0. −12 < −5, but |−12| > |−5|, so a balance of −$12 is the bigger debt.

items.q: What is |−8|?
items.e: Absolute value is the distance from 0. −8 is 8 units from 0, so |−8| = 8. An absolute value is never negative.

items.q: What is |15|?
items.e: 15 is positive and is 15 units from 0, so |15| = 15. The absolute value of a positive number is the number itself.

items.q: What is |−2.5|?
items.e: Absolute value is the distance from 0. −2.5 is 2.5 units from 0, so |−2.5| = 2.5. An absolute value is never negative.

items.q: Compare |−2.5| and |−6|. Which statement is true?
Which numbers have an absolute value of 2.5?
items.e: Both 2.5 and −2.5 are 2.5 units from 0, so |2.5| = 2.5 and |−2.5| = 2.5.

items.q:
Which number has the least absolute value?
−0.5,  2,  −1.5,  1
items.e: Find each distance from 0: |−0.5| = 0.5, |2| = 2, |−1.5| = 1.5, |1| = 1. The least is 0.5, so the answer is −0.5. The least absolute value is the number closest to 0, not the least number.

items.q:
Which number has the greatest absolute value?
4,  −12,  10,  −6
items.e: Find each distance from 0: |4| = 4, |−12| = 12, |10| = 10, |−6| = 6. The greatest is 12, so the answer is −12. The greatest absolute value is the number farthest from 0, not the greatest number.

items.q: Compare |−7| and |7|. Which statement is true?
items.e: |−7| = 7 and |7| = 7. Opposites are the same distance from 0, so |−7| = |7|.

items.q: Jack says the number with the greater absolute value is always the greater number. Is he right?
c: Yes. It is true for every number.
items.e: It is not true for negative numbers. −8 is farther from 0 than 3, so |−8| > |3|. But −8 is to the left of 3, so −8 < 3.

sets.title: Absolute value and order word problems

items.q: At 7 a.m., it was −4 °F in Fargo and 2 °F in Omaha. Which statement is true?
items.e: −4 is to the left of 2 on a thermometer number line, so −4 < 2. The lower temperature is colder: Fargo was colder.

items.q: The low temperatures for four days were: Monday −3 °C, Tuesday −8 °C, Wednesday 1 °C, Thursday −5 °C. Which day was the coldest?
items.e: The coldest day has the least temperature. From least to greatest: −8 °C, −5 °C, −3 °C, 1 °C. −8 °C is the least, so Tuesday was the coldest.

items.q: A freezer must stay colder than −5 °F. Which temperature is colder than −5 °F?
items.e: Colder means less. −7 < −5, because −7 is to the left of −5. So −7 °F is colder. (−3 > −5, so −3 °F is warmer.)

items.q: Luis’s bank account balance is −$30. Eli’s balance is −$20. Who owes more money?
c: Luis, because −$30 is a debt of $30
Eli, because −$20 is a debt of $20
items.e: A negative balance is a debt. |−30| = 30, so Luis owes $30. |−20| = 20, so Eli owes $20. Luis owes more, even though −$30 < −$20.

items.q: Which account balance shows a debt of more than $25?
items.e: A balance of −$30 is a debt of $30, and 30 > 25. −$20 is a debt of $20, −$25 is a debt of exactly $25, and $30 is not a debt. A balance less than −$25 means a debt greater than $25.

items.q: Mia’s account balance is −$45. How much money does she owe?
items.e: A negative balance is a debt. The size of the debt is the absolute value: |−45| = 45. She owes $45.

items.q: Four friends have these account balances: $15, −$40, −$10, $0. Order the balances from least to greatest.
items.e: The biggest debt is the least balance. From least to greatest: −$40, −$10, $0, $15. −$40 < −$10 because a debt of $40 is more than a debt of $10.

items.q: A diver is at −40 feet. A submarine is at −120 feet. Which one is deeper?
c: They are at the same depth
items.e: Deeper means lower. −120 is to the left of (below) −40, so −120 < −40. The submarine is deeper: 120 feet below sea level.

items.q: A fish is swimming at an elevation of −18 feet. How far below sea level is it?
items.e: Sea level is 0. The distance from 0 is the absolute value: |−18| = 18. The fish is 18 feet below sea level.

items.q: A bird is flying at 25 feet. A fish is swimming at −30 feet. Which one is farther from sea level?
c: They are the same distance from sea level
The bird, because it is above sea level
items.e: Distance from sea level is absolute value. |−30| = 30 and |25| = 25. 30 > 25, so the fish is farther from sea level, even though 25 > −30.

items.q: Four places have these elevations: a beach at 0 feet; a valley at −86 feet; a hill at 120 feet; a mine tunnel at −250 feet. Which place is the lowest?
items.e: The lowest place has the least elevation. −250 < −86 < 0 < 120, so the mine tunnel is the lowest.

items.q: In golf, the lowest score wins. Sam’s score is −3. Nora’s score is −1. Who wins?
items.e: −3 is to the left of −1, so −3 < −1. The lowest score wins, so Sam wins.

items.q: In golf, a lower score is better. Four players scored −2, 1, −5, 0. Order the scores from best to worst.
items.e: Best to worst means least to greatest: −5, −2, 0, 1. −5 is the best score because it is the least.

items.q: At noon, the temperature was −6 °F. At midnight, it was −11 °F. Which statement is true?
c: −11 > −6, so it was colder at noon
−6 < −11, so it was colder at noon
−11 > −6, so it was colder at midnight
−11 < −6, so it was colder at midnight
items.e: −11 °F is farther below 0 than −6 °F, so −11 < −6. The lower temperature is colder: midnight.

items.q: One morning, it was −9 °F in Anchorage and −2 °F in Denver. Which city’s temperature was closer to 0 °F?
c: They were the same distance from 0 °F
items.e: Closer to 0 means the smaller absolute value. |−9| = 9 and |−2| = 2. 2 < 9, so Denver was closer to 0 °F.

items.q: In a football game, a team gained 5 yards on one play (+5) and lost 7 yards on the next play (−7). On which play did the ball move a greater distance?
c: The first play, because a gain is always more
Both plays moved the ball the same distance
items.e: Distance is absolute value: |5| = 5 and |−7| = 7. 7 > 5, so the ball moved farther on the second play, even though 5 > −7.

items.q: Owen has a balance of −$12, Grace has $3, Ava has −$40, and Maya has $0. Who has the greatest balance?
items.e: The greatest balance is the one farthest right on a number line: −$40 < −$12 < $0 < $3. Grace has the greatest balance, $3. Ava has the greatest debt, not the most money.

items.q: Thermometer A shows −2.5 °C. Thermometer B shows −1.5 °C. Which thermometer shows the colder temperature?
items.e: −2.5 is to the left of −1.5, so −2.5 < −1.5. The lower temperature is colder: Thermometer A.

items.q: The low temperature on Monday was −7 °F. On Tuesday, the low was even colder. Which could be Tuesday’s low?
items.e: Colder means less than −7, so the number must be to the left of −7. −9 < −7, so −9 °F could be Tuesday’s low. −5 °F is warmer, because −5 > −7.

items.q: Omar’s account balance is less than −$50. What does this tell you about his debt?
c: He does not owe any money
items.e: A balance less than −$50 is to the left of −$50, like −$60. That is farther from 0, so the debt is more than $50.
